findings.description: `host.endswith(domain)` accepts any host whose name merely ends with the partner domain string. With partner domain `shop.example`, an attacker-registered host such as `evilshop.example` or `notshop.example` passes. The policy then reflects that origin with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, so the attacker's page can read member balances and redeem rewards using the victim's session cookie.
findings.suggestion: Require an exact match or a subdomain boundary: `host == domain or host.endswith('.' + domain)`.
findings.title: Partner domain match uses endswith without a dot boundary

findings.description: For the partner check only the scheme, hostname, path and query are validated. An origin like `https://user@shop.example` or one with an arbitrary port is accepted and reflected verbatim in Access-Control-Allow-Origin. Real browser Origin headers never contain userinfo, so such values only come from non-browser clients. Reflecting unvalidated text makes the check looser than intended.
findings.suggestion: Reject origins where `parts.username` or `parts.password` is set, and decide explicitly whether to allow a port. Alternatively, compare against a rebuilt `https://hostname[:port]` string.
findings.title: Origin with userinfo or port is not validated
